    SEICAT socio-economic impact classification

    Source: R/inv-niche.R
    inv_seicat_score.Rd

    Assigns each alien taxon its Socio-Economic Impact Classification of Alien Taxa (SEICAT) category from a table of impact records (Bacher et al. 2018), the counterpart of inv_eicat_score() for impacts on human well-being (safety, material and immaterial assets, health, and social, spiritual and cultural relations). As in the IUCN scheme, the category is the most severe magnitude recorded: Minimal Concern (MC), Minor (MN), Moderate (MO), Major (MR) or Massive (MV); MO and above are harmful.

    Usage

    inv_seicat_score(
  .data,
  species,
  magnitude,
  mechanism = NULL,
  confidence = NULL
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame with one row per impact record.

    species

    <tidy-select> Column with the taxon.

    magnitude

    <tidy-select> Column with the impact magnitude, as codes ("MC", "MN", "MO", "MR", "MV", "DD") or names ("Minimal Concern", "Minor", "Moderate", "Major", "Massive", "Data Deficient"), in any case.

    mechanism

    <tidy-select> Optional column with the constituent of well-being affected.

    confidence

    <tidy-select> Optional column with the confidence of each record ("low", "medium", "high").

    Value

    As inv_eicat_score(), with seicat_category and seicat_score.

    References

    Bacher, S., Blackburn, T. M., Essl, F., Genovesi, P., Heikkila, J., Jeschke, J. M., Jones, G., Keller, R., Kenis, M., Kueffer, C., Martinou, A. F., Nentwig, W., Pergl, J., Pysek, P., Rabitsch, W., Richardson, D. M., Roy, H. E., Saul, W.-C., Scalera, R., Vila, M., Wilson, J. R. U. and Kumschick, S. (2018). Socio-economic impact classification of alien taxa (SEICAT). Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 9, 159-168. doi:10.1111/2041-210X.12844

    Examples

    records <- data.frame(
  species = c("sp01", "sp01", "sp02", "sp03"),
  magnitude = c("MN", "MR", "MC", "DD"),
  mechanism = c("health", "material assets", "safety", "health")
)
inv_seicat_score(records, species, magnitude, mechanism)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 9
#>   species n_records seicat_category seicat_score harmful max_mechanisms 
#>   <chr>       <int> <ord>                  <int> <lgl>   <chr>          
#> 1 sp01            2 MR                         4 TRUE    material assets
#> 2 sp02            1 MC                         1 FALSE   safety         
#> 3 sp03            1 DD                        NA FALSE   NA             
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: confidence <chr>, n_mechanisms <int>,
#> #   cumulative_score <dbl>
